summary: The S. 933, NASA Transition Authorization Act of 2025, authorizes funding for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for fiscal year 2025 at a level of $25,507,540,000 across its various mission directorates. The bill reauthorizes and updates numerous NASA programs related to space exploration, low-Earth orbit operations, space technology, aeronautics, science, and STEM education, while introducing new requirements for commercial partnerships, safety measures, and interagency coordination.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new talent exchange programs, enhanced internal core competency requirements for spacesuit design, and mentoring and workforce tracking policies.

Eligible to participate in competitive solicitations for commercial low-Earth orbit destinations, lunar landing systems, spacesuit capabilities, commercial lunar payload services, and prototype project follow-on contracts.
affected_groups.group: Commercial space providers and aerospace industry

affected_groups.effect: Impacted through reauthorizations of the National Space Grant College and Fellowship Program, skilled technical workforce education outreach, and higher education research collaborations.
affected_groups.group: Students, academic institutions, and educational consortia

key_provisions: Authorizes $25,507,540,000 for NASA appropriations in fiscal year 2025 across multiple mission directorates and offices.

Directs NASA to maintain continuous human presence in low-Earth orbit through the ISS and future commercial space stations, requires a de-orbit vehicle for the ISS, and establishes a Commercial Low-Earth Orbit Development Program.

Reaffirms support for the Artemis program, Moon to Mars architecture, the Space Launch System, Orion crew vehicle, human-rated lunar landing capabilities, and advanced spacesuit capabilities managed through the Johnson Space Center.
Authorizes the continuation of aeronautics research into hypersonic technologies, advanced air mobility, unmanned aircraft systems, hydrogen aviation, and emergency response operations for wildfires.

Maintains balanced science portfolios, directs a Mars Sample Return program using firm fixed-price industry agreements, mandates policies for commercial satellite data acquisition, and establishes the Planetary Defense Coordination Office.
Implements a temporary public-private talent exchange program permitting the assignment of NASA and private sector employees for up to three years under strict ethics and anti-conflict rules.

Restricts Federal funds from being used by NASA, OSTP, or NSpC to coordinate bilaterally with China or host official Chinese visitors unless specific national security and human rights certifications are met.

The bill reauthorizes and updates numerous NASA programs related to space exploration, low-Earth orbit operations, space technology, aeronautics, science, and STEM education, while introducing new requirements for commercial partnerships, safety measures, and interagency coordination.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes sweeping policy direction and funding authorizations for the nation's civil space and aeronautics programs for fiscal year 2025, shaping long-term strategic transitions from government-led space operations to commercial markets.
